cases.prompt: Perform a functional test of the overlay-window on the Settings screen to uncover potential errors. I only want the focused test and findings for now.
cases.trap: Create durable workflow state merely because the user asked Loom to perform a bounded read-only test.
expectations: Keeps the focused function test outside durable workflow state unless the user explicitly asks for tracked/governed verification.
Selects a bounded read-only investigation, directly or delegated, with findings as its deliverable; does not fabricate test results in this decision-only context.
Does not require Designer merely because the tested surface is visual; no new UX meaning has been requested.
must_not: Must not call loom_start/loom_route or broaden the request into a full UI/UX or product-readiness workflow solely for this conversational test.

cases.prompt: Debug the call going from the frontend to the backend. It returns 401. Find where it goes wrong; don't redesign auth.
cases.trap: Turn an ordinary diagnosis request into a Task workflow, or redesign authentication instead of tracing the failure.
expectations: Keeps the diagnosis outside durable workflow state by default and investigates the concrete 401 cause conversationally.
Uses Diagnostic as an advisory conversational capability if fresh tracing/reproduction materially improves causal confidence.
Does not involve Architect, Specifier, Planner, Critic, or Product Acceptance unless the user later commits to work that actually requires those authorities.
must_not: Must not call loom_start/loom_route merely because diagnosis may require tools, and must not redesign authentication merely because auth code is involved.

cases.prompt: Review this retry helper for error-handling mistakes and tell me what is wrong. No code changes yet.
cases.trap: Turn a focused findings-only code review into governed execution.
expectations: Keeps the focused review outside durable workflow state and returns findings/evidence conversationally.
Does not silently turn review findings into implementation work because the user explicitly asked for no code changes.
Does not introduce Anchor, Planner, Critic, Product Acceptance, or Task workflow ceremony unless the user later commits to tracked execution.
must_not: Must not call loom_start/loom_route or create a new Anchor for the focused review.

cases.prompt: Verify that this one endpoint was migrated from /api/v1/widgets to /api/v2/widgets and that the response mapping is still correct.
cases.trap: Turn a bounded read-only verification question into a durable workflow without a request for tracked/governed verification.
expectations: Keeps the endpoint verification conversational by default and inspects only the relevant caller, mapping, and focused evidence.
Uses Research conversationally only if current external API documentation is actually needed.
Does not create Task/Planner/whole-product acceptance state unless the user explicitly asks to track/preserve/govern the verification.
must_not: Must not call loom_start/loom_route or expand the investigation into auditing every API migration without evidence or a user request.

cases.prompt: The accepted UI spec already says this button label is 'Retry'. Change the current 'Try again' label to 'Retry' and run the relevant tests.
cases.trap: Route to Designer just because visible UI text changes.
expectations: Treats the edit as Task depth because the user-facing meaning is already fully specified.
Routes directly to bounded implementation plus verification.
Does not set new human-facing authority merely because a visible string changes mechanically.
must_not: Must not ask Designer to re-decide wording that accepted authority already fixes.

cases.prompt: The delete button currently removes the item immediately. Change it so users can recover accidental deletions on this screen, but the product docs do not say whether that means undo, confirmation, trash, or something else. The bounded recovery outcome is committed; I have not reserved the interaction mechanism for myself.
cases.trap: Stay shallow and let Worker invent new recovery UX semantics.
expectations: Promotes the work to Change depth because new user-facing recovery semantics are unresolved.
Routes the missing UX meaning to Designer and behavioral guarantees to Specifier when needed before implementation.
Still avoids full Objective ceremony unless later evidence shows the work is broad enough to need decomposition and whole-product acceptance.
must_not: Must not send the request directly to Worker to choose confirmation versus undo versus trash.
Must not start intent-grilling merely because the bounded change needs Designer/Specifier authority; specialist-owned realization is resolved inside Change depth.

cases.prompt: A focused 401 investigation found that one shared auth adapter mixes service identity and user identity across seven callers. Existing authority defines the intended identity semantics, but the adapter boundary must be redesigned. Fix it.
cases.trap: Either keep Task depth despite a demonstrated cross-cutting structural boundary, or jump all the way to a full Objective without need.
expectations: Promotes from Task to Change depth based on the new material structural evidence.
Routes structural realization to Architect, preserves the completed diagnostic evidence, then implements and reviews the bounded repair.
Does not require Planner, holistic Critic, or whole-product Product Acceptance solely because seven callers share the adapter.
must_not: Must not discard/repeat the completed diagnosis or classify the work as Objective merely from file count.

cases.prompt: Build saved views across the dashboard: users can create, rename, delete, share team views, set a default, and migrate existing local filters. This spans frontend, backend persistence, API contracts, permissions, UX, and rollout. State the appropriate depth, immediate action, and delivery path through product verification.
cases.trap: Under-route a broad multi-part product feature as a small Change.
expectations: Classifies this as Objective depth because it is broad multi-part product delivery requiring decomposition and whole-product verification.

Commits to accepted product authority, the necessary specialist/review path, decomposition, implementation, and whole-product Product Acceptance. Equivalent descriptions of these stages count; exact stage-name recitation is not required.
Does not squeeze the feature into one direct Worker task or claim later stages already occurred.
must_not: Must not choose Task or Change depth merely to minimize ceremony when decomposition is clearly useful.

cases.prompt: You started a Task to function-test an overlay. The test found one missing null check in a local click handler; expected behavior is already specified and the fix is one bounded edit with an existing regression test. Continue.
cases.trap: Escalate just because the test found a defect.
expectations: Stays at Task depth because the finding has an obvious bounded fix and introduces no new product/design/architecture authority.

Continues bounded Worker repair and independent Reviewer verification without adding new Designer/Specifier/Architect authority, Planner, Critic, or whole-product Product Acceptance. The Task Reviewer is required verification, not forbidden extra ceremony.
must_not: Must not promote to Change or Objective solely because an error was discovered.

cases.prompt: You started a Task to test an overlay. Evidence now shows keyboard focus is lost because three overlay types implement conflicting close/focus semantics, and the product docs do not define which element should regain focus. Continue.
cases.trap: Keep Task depth even though the finding exposes missing cross-component UX/behavior semantics.
expectations: Promotes to Change depth because current evidence now shows unresolved user-facing and behavioral meaning.
Routes the missing focus/recovery semantics to Designer and/or Specifier before Worker changes the shared behavior.
Preserves the useful test evidence from the original Task rather than restarting unrelated work.
must_not: Must not let Worker invent focus-restoration semantics.

cases.prompt: A focused readiness review uncovered that our auth model, API ownership rules, five screens, and persistence assumptions all need coordinated redesign. I have reviewed the findings and now say: 'Yes, these findings are substantial; fix them properly.'
cases.trap: Either remain shallow despite demonstrated broad scope, or escalate only because the user said 'substantial' without considering evidence.
expectations: Uses the demonstrated cross-system breadth, together with the user's new implementation request, to classify the follow-up as Objective depth.
Shapes/uses accepted product authority as needed, then uses planning and whole-product verification appropriate to the broad redesign.
Treats the prior review evidence as input rather than repeating the entire discovery exercise.
must_not: Must not cite the word 'substantial' alone as the reason for Objective depth; the cross-system evidence is load-bearing.

cases.prompt: Check why this one unit test fails. It might turn out to reveal a giant architecture problem, I have no idea.
cases.trap: Preemptively create a Task or architecture workflow because the user speculates that the cause might be large.
expectations: Keeps the failing-test investigation conversational initially and investigates the concrete failure.
Treats possible future architecture complexity as speculation, not current routing evidence.
Crosses into Task/Change/Objective only if the user later commits to tracked execution and current evidence warrants that depth.
must_not: Must not call loom_start/loom_route, Architect, Planner, or full Objective ceremony based only on 'might'.

cases.prompt: Check that the shell allowlist rejects unsafe inline environment assignments. This is a focused security regression check. Do not change policy; if you find a policy defect, report it and stop.
cases.trap: Assume a focused read-only security check automatically requires durable workflow state, maximum ceremony, or implicit repair authority.
expectations: Keeps the focused security regression check conversational unless tracked/governed verification was explicitly requested.
Does not add architecture/product ceremony merely because the domain is security-sensitive.
If the check proves a defect, reports it first; later execution depth depends on the user's committed follow-up and demonstrated authority needs.
must_not: Must not call loom_start/loom_route or classify security subject matter alone as Objective depth.
Must not treat discovery of a policy defect as authorization to repair it.

cases.prompt: Debug why the export command hangs after writing the file. I only want the root cause and evidence; do not fix it yet. No source, trace, or runtime observations have been supplied. Decide the next action.
cases.trap: Create a Task or automatically continue into repair despite an explicit diagnosis-only boundary.
expectations: Keeps the diagnosis outside durable workflow state and selects bounded causal inspection or foreground Diagnostic investigation to obtain the missing source/trace evidence.

Commits to returning confirmed findings or a precise remaining evidence gap without pretending the cause is already established. In this decision-only case, a concrete investigation decision is sufficient; unavailable completed findings are not required.
Stops at findings because the user explicitly excluded repair; a later fix request would cross the execution boundary.
must_not: Must not call loom_start/loom_route or dispatch implementation repair unless the user later asks for tracked execution.
Must not invent a hang cause from the symptom alone.

cases.prompt: Set up a tracked investigation of why the frontend request returns 401. Preserve the root-cause evidence and have the findings independently verified, but do not fix anything.
cases.trap: Treat an explicitly tracked/governed read-only investigation as casual conversation, or route it through mutation/product ceremony.
expectations: Starts a bounded request workflow before broad investigation and routes it at Task depth with diagnosis enabled and implementation disabled.
Dispatches Diagnostic to establish that the frontend sends X-Access-Token while the backend requires an Authorization: Bearer token, causing the 401.
After Diagnostic returns, immediately continues the governed workflow through the read-only Reviewer verification gate rather than stopping at findings.
Preserves the root-cause findings through the read-only Reviewer verification path.
must_not: Must not route the tracked diagnosis through Worker implementation or Objective ceremony.

# Saved Views Anchor

**Status:** accepted

## Goal
Deliver saved views across frontend, backend, permissions, API contracts, migration and rollout. Users create, rename, delete, share team views, set a default, and migrate existing local filters.

## Accepted product decisions
A saved view contains a name, filters, sort order, and visible columns. Personal views belong to their creator and are private. A creator may share a view with their current team; team members may read/apply shared views, but only the creator or a team administrator may rename/delete them. No public links or cross-team access are allowed. Defaults are per-user and must reference a view that user may access. Deleting a view never deletes underlying records; a missing default falls back to the built-in view.

Existing browser-local filters migrate into a private personal view after sign-in. Migration must not lose the original local filters or create duplicates on retry. Rollout uses an opt-in feature flag and preserves the old local-filter experience until enabled; rollback must retain created view data. Offline multi-device synchronization and concurrent collaborative editing are excluded.

## Observable success
Real frontend/API/persistence paths demonstrate create, rename, share, apply, default selection, deletion, permission denial, restart persistence, and retry-safe migration. The legacy filter experience still works when the feature is disabled.

## Specialist realization
Interaction details, validation/error presentation, API shape, storage schema, and technical rollout realization remain for the owning specialists within these accepted outcomes. No new user choice is needed merely to choose those mechanisms.
